subject: botany
question_text: Which group of plants is called amphibians of the plant kingdom? Name the branch of Botany which deals with them.

verification.note: Sourced from the Telangana Junior Fastrack botany guide, Chapter 3 'Science of Plants' (book pp.5-6). The botany book prints NO star ranks and NO year citations, so stars=0 and appearances=[] record absence of signal, not measured frequency. Only ONE botany source is held — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand is physics-only and no botany board paper exists in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the board-paper back-test are both structurally impossible for botany: 'unverified' means never yet checkable against a second source, not checked-and-clean. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Amphibians of the plant kingdom
lines: Bryophytes are called the amphibians of the
plant kingdom. They grow on moist soil (land)
but need water for sexual reproduction.
steps.why: Amphibians live both on land and in water; bryophytes carry the same name because the plant grows on land while fertilisation still needs water.
common_mistakes: Answering algae — algae live fully in water; the group that needs both land and water is the bryophytes.
Giving the group without the reason — one line on the water need makes the answer complete.
steps.memory_tip: Frogs live on land but breed in water; mosses do the same — so bryophytes are called amphibians.
steps.margin_note: Group name plus the water-for-reproduction reason.

steps.label: The branch
steps.why: The branch again comes from the group name: bryo- plus -logy gives bryology.
common_mistakes: Swapping with pteridology — pteridology is ferns; bryology is mosses and liverworts.
steps.margin_note: The boxed arrow line completes the answer.

insider_note: The board asks this in the same two-part shape every time — group first, branch second; answer in two labelled lines.
